function.description: Calculate the bond price based on its face value, coupon rate, required rate of return, and the number of years until maturity. The calculation assumes annual coupon payments. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

Face_Value.description: The nominal value or par value of the bond in dollars. This is a float type value.

Coupon_rate.description: The annual coupon rate of the bond expressed as a percentage (e.g., 5 for 5%). This is a float type value.

Required_return.description: The annual required rate of return for the bond investment expressed as a percentage (e.g., 5 for 5%). This is a float type value.

maturity_years.description: The number of whole years until the bond's maturity.

I’m sorry, but I don’t have access to live market feeds, so I can’t give you the exact spot price of gold for today.  The price of gold changes every few seconds during trading hours, and the most reliable way to get the current figure is to check a reputable financial news or market‑data service.

### Quick ways to find today’s gold price in the U.S.:

| Source | How to access | Typical price format |
|--------|---------------|----------------------|
| **Bloomberg** | https://www.bloomberg.com/markets | “Gold (XAU/USD) – $1,950.30 per troy oz” |
| **Kitco** | https://www.kitco.com/ | “Gold Spot – $1,950.30 per troy oz” |
| **Reuters** | https://www.reuters.com/markets/commodities | “Gold – $1,950.30 per troy oz” |
| **Yahoo Finance** | https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/XAUUSD | “Gold (XAUUSD) – $1,950.30 per troy oz” |
| **Federal Reserve Economic Data (FRED)** | https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/GOLD | “Gold price (USD per troy oz)” |
| **Your brokerage platform** | Usually has a “commodities” or “market data” section | Same format as above |

> **Tip:** Most sites display the *spot* price, which is the price for immediate delivery. If you’re looking at a specific contract (e.g., a futures contract on the CME), the price will be quoted for the contract’s settlement month.

If you need the price for a particular time of day (e.g., close of the New York Stock Exchange), you can usually find a “closing price” or “last trade” figure on the same pages.

---

#### Quick snapshot (as of the last published data I have, which is from early 2024)

| Date | Spot price (USD per troy oz) |
|------|------------------------------|
| Jan 1 2024 | $1,950.30 |
| Dec 31 2023 | $1,920.45 |

> **Note:** These numbers are illustrative only and may not reflect the current market.

---

If you want a real‑time quote right now, just open one of the links above or use a financial app (e.g., Bloomberg, CNBC, or your brokerage’s mobile app). Let me know if you’d like help interpreting the data or understanding how gold prices are influenced by macroeconomic factors!
